raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" with a three-layered architecture. The "Observe" layer uses lightweight desktop sensors to capture work patterns (application usage, activity sequences, time allocation). The "Intelligence Layer" acts as a "Brain" to detect employee intent, business value of tasks, and "drift" in workflows. The "Execution Layer" is an "Agent Factory" that automates the generation, deployment, and monitoring of AI agents for high-ROI opportunities, complete with built-in approval gates. It leverages existing foundation models, focusing on understanding the "Work Graph" to identify automation opportunities and assist work mid-flow.
raw.thesis: narma proposes an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an Observe layer to capture work patterns, an Intelligence layer to detect intent and work drift, and an Execution layer ("Agent Factory") to automatically generate and deploy AI agents. The venture aims to help AI-first companies identify and deploy high-ROI AI automation at scale by revealing where resources are inefficiently used and where AI can intervene. This is an offering that complements existing AI solutions by providing a meta-layer for observing, reasoning about, and automating work within enterprises. The founder seems to envision a growth-oriented startup given the emphasis on "scale" and "continuous AI lift." They are currently at the idea stage, as evidenced by the descriptive language without mention of a built product or users. The venture directly addresses a critical pain point for AI-first companies: the struggle to pinpoint AI savings, measure ROI, and manage system and human resource drift.
things_that_must_work: Seamless integration with various desktop applications and enterprise systems for data capture.
Accurate and reliable detection of employee intent and business value of tasks by the 'Brain'.
Effective and safe generation, deployment, and monitoring of AI agents by the 'Agent Factory' within enterprise environments.
Robust security and privacy measures given the sensitive nature of observing work patterns.
User acceptance and adoption of detailed work pattern observation and automated AI interventions.
